claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can reduce the sintering temperature of ceramic or powder-based materials by 200°C relative to conventional sintering.
The starting material is a green body or powder.
The proposed SPS treatment uses a pulse current of 1000 A.
The proposed SPS treatment applies a uniaxial pressure of 50 MPa.
The SPS process is conducted under vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
SPS promotes neck formation between particles.
The applied electrical field and pressure enhance mass transport.
The applied electrical field and pressure enhance densification.
Enhanced mass transport and densification permit a 200°C reduction in sintering temperature.
The magnitude of the temperature reduction varies with the specific material and SPS parameters.
A reduction below 200°C may not be achievable for all ceramic or powder-based materials.
Failure of SPS to reduce the sintering temperature by at least 150°C falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The central prediction specifies a 200°C reduction, but the experiment only falsifies reductions below 150°C. A measured reduction of 150–199°C would fail the stated 200°C prediction while not falsifying the hypothesis under the proposed rule.

The boundary says that reductions below 200°C may be unachievable, whereas the uncertainty statement implies that reductions may vary around the 200°C prediction. The boundary wording appears directionally inconsistent and may have intended to say that a full 200°C reduction is not always achievable.
